solution: Colours are only ever copied, so the set of live colours can shrink but never grow: a necessary condition is that every colour of t already occurs in s (and for n = 1, s = t). For a connected graph with n >= 2 that is also sufficient, and the witness is built in two phases. Phase A repairs the colour multiset: while some colour occurs fewer times than t needs, take a vertex whose colour is in surplus, BFS to the nearest vertex whose colour is in deficit, and walk the surplus one edge at a time toward it, each move being a single vertex copying a neighbour; only surplus vertices are overwritten, so no needed colour is ever lost, and each unit of deficit costs at most one shortest path. Phase B permutes: with the multiset correct, match holders to targets and realise that permutation by adjacent swaps on a spanning tree, peeling leaves in reverse DFS order so the working part stays connected - a swap is one legal step because the update is simultaneous and both endpoints read the other's old colour. O(n^3) work, O(n) steps per repair, comfortably inside 20000 steps.
statement_summary: Each vertex of a connected undirected graph carries one of k colours, and in one step every vertex simultaneously either keeps its colour or takes the colour of a neighbour. Given a starting and a target colouring on at most a hundred vertices with at most a hundred colours, the task is to decide reachability and, when reachable, print a witness sequence of at most twenty thousand steps.
notes: The feasibility criterion was checked exhaustively by BFS over the whole configuration space of every connected graph on 2..4 vertices with k <= 3, against every (s,t) pair, and the constructor was replayed step by step on 300 random small instances plus adversarial n=100 paths, stars, cycles and random trees: worst observed 3614 steps against the 20000 budget. The simultaneity of the step is the crux - a 3-vertex star with s=(c,A,B) and target (*,B,A) is unreachable by one-vertex-at-a-time copies but easy in three simultaneous steps, so a solution that only ever moves one colour at a time along a path will wrongly report Impossible. Not labelled simulation: nothing is simulated forward, the sequence is constructed.
